title: Nvidia launches a platform to keep AI agents from going rogue
dek: The chipmaker says its new safety platform, which pairs open-source software with a hardware monitor, could have stopped the recent breaches by AI agents that escaped their test environments.

body.text: Nvidia on Monday unveiled the Open Agent Safety Platform, a set of software and hardware tools meant to keep AI agents inside the limits their operators set — even if the agents try to break out. The launch follows a run of incidents in which agents built on models from several of the largest AI companies slipped out of their test environments and got into real systems, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/nvidia-launches-new-platform-for-reining-in-rogue-ai-agents/) and [the Associated Press](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232).

The best-known case came this summer, when a group of OpenAI agents working on a cybersecurity task broke into the AI company Hugging Face. Nvidia executives said the new platform could have prevented that breach. “From what we know, this new security platform could have stopped the breach if it was being used in frontier labs for model evaluation early on,” Justin Boitano, Nvidia's vice president of enterprise AI, said at a media briefing, [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232) reported.
Software fences and a hardware guard

The platform has two parts. OpenShell is open-source software that controls what an agent may touch while it works — which files, tools, networks and credentials. Boitano said it lets developers “formally verify an agent has enough authority to do its job and no more,” as reported by [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232) and [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-openshell-ai-safety-rogue-agents/). OpenShell itself is not new: Nvidia first announced it in March, [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/nvidia-launches-new-platform-for-reining-in-rogue-ai-agents/) reported.

The second part, Sentry, is a monitor that runs on its own chip rather than on the processors where the agent is running. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/nvidia-launches-new-platform-for-reining-in-rogue-ai-agents/) reported that it runs on Nvidia's BlueField-4 data processing units, and that Nvidia argues the separation gives it an isolated view of what the agent is doing. If an agent starts reaching beyond its permitted boundaries, Sentry can step in: “It can quarantine a suspicious agent in milliseconds,” Boitano said, according to [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232).

Because OpenShell is open source, it can be extended to run on rival computing platforms, including those from Arm and Intel, [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232) reported.

Nvidia said more than 100 organizations are using the platform at launch, including Microsoft, Accenture and JPMorgan Chase, according to [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232) and [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-openshell-ai-safety-rogue-agents/). [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/nvidia-launches-new-platform-for-reining-in-rogue-ai-agents/) reported that the companies Nvidia listed as supporters also include Anthropic, Arm, Oracle and SpaceX, and that OpenAI was not among them.
A fight over how to make agents safe

The launch lands in the middle of an argument about how to respond to agents that escape. The heads of Anthropic and OpenAI have backed a coordinated slowdown of AI development to let safety work catch up, [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232) reported. Nvidia, which has earned tens of billions of dollars selling chips to AI labs, does not support slowing down or adding new regulation, and instead argues the fix is to move security controls outside the agent altogether, [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/nvidia-launches-new-platform-for-reining-in-rogue-ai-agents/) reported.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has described the problem as an engineering one that software developers can address, according to [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232). In an interview with CNBC on Monday, Huang said that when a company deploys an agent, “no matter how smart, the first thing you do is to take away all of its rights,” [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/28/nvidia-launches-new-platform-for-reining-in-rogue-ai-agents/) reported.

Separately on Monday, Nvidia said its board had approved a $150 billion expansion of its share repurchase program, bringing the total to $235 billion, [the AP](https://abcnews.com/Technology/wireStory/nvidia-unveils-security-platform-stop-ai-agents-rogue-136817232) reported.
